options.D: Set Up Slide Show → 'Browsed at a kiosk (full screen)' / loop continuously

questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: Kiosk mode loops the show automatically.

questions.question: During a slide show, typing a slide number and pressing Enter:
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: This is a quick way to navigate.

questions.question: Which PowerPoint feature groups related slides, e.g. 'Introduction', 'Results', to organise a large presentation?
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: Sections appear in the slide thumbnail pane.

questions.question: Ctrl+G in PowerPoint:
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: Ctrl+Shift+G ungroups them.

questions.question: A presentation can be exported from PowerPoint as:

options.A: A PDF or an MP4 video

questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: File → Export offers PDF and video options.

questions.question: SmartArt in PowerPoint is used to:

options.C: Insert diagrams such as processes, cycles and hierarchies

questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: SmartArt converts bullet text into diagrams.

questions.question: In PowerPoint, which view shows the slide in a window with simple controls, useful for reviewing without full-screen mode?
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: Reading View is on the View tab and the status bar.

questions.question: The Morph transition in modern PowerPoint:

options.C: Animates smooth movement of matching objects from one slide to the next

questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: It creates movement effects between similar slides.

questions.question: Esc during a slide show:
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: It returns to the editing view.

questions.question: A custom slide show lets you:

options.C: Present a selected subset of slides in a chosen order from the same file

questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: Useful when presenting to different audiences.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Transitions are applied between slides.
II. Animations can be applied to individual text boxes and images.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: Both are correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Changing the font in the Slide Master changes it on all slides using that master.
Reason (R): PowerPoint presentations are saved with the .pptx extension by default.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: Both are true, but R is unrelated; the real reason is that slide layouts inherit formatting from the Slide Master.

questions.question: Which tab contains the Rehearse Timings, Custom Slide Show and Set Up Slide Show commands?
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: They are all on the Slide Show tab.

questions.question: Ctrl+D applied to a selected slide thumbnail in PowerPoint:
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: It creates a copy immediately after the original.

questions.question: A template file in PowerPoint has the extension:
questions.subject: PowerPoint Presentation
questions.explanation: Templates store themes, layouts and sample content.

sets.name: 1 · Typical Configuration of a Computer System

questions.question: In the specification 'Intel Core i5-12400', the number 12 indicates the processor's:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: The first digits after the brand modifier give the generation (12th gen).

questions.question: In Intel processor names, the suffix 'K' (e.g. i7-13700K) means:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: 'F' means no integrated graphics; 'U' low-power mobile; 'H' high-performance mobile.

questions.question: A processor listed as '6 cores, 12 threads' supports:

options.B: Simultaneous multithreading (e.g. Intel Hyper-Threading), running two threads per core

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: SMT lets each physical core execute two hardware threads.

questions.question: What is the peak bandwidth of one channel of DDR4-3200 memory with a 64-bit bus?
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: 3200 million transfers/s × 8 bytes = 25,600 MB/s = 25.6 GB/s; dual channel doubles it.

questions.question: A 32-bit operating system can directly address at most about:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: 2^32 bytes = 4 GB; 64-bit systems are needed for more RAM.

questions.question: USB 2.0 has a maximum signalling rate of:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: USB 1.1 = 12 Mbps; USB 3.0 (3.2 Gen 1) = 5 Gbps; USB 3.2 Gen 2 = 10 Gbps.

questions.question: USB 3.2 Gen 1 (originally USB 3.0) supports up to:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: USB 3.2 Gen 2x2 reaches 20 Gbps and USB4 up to 40 Gbps.

questions.question: Wi-Fi 6 corresponds to the IEEE standard:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi 4 = 802.11n, Wi-Fi 5 = 802.11ac; 802.3 is Ethernet.

questions.question: A 'Gigabit Ethernet' port supports a speed of:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: It uses an RJ-45 connector with Cat 5e or better cable.

questions.question: Which Windows tool shows a detailed report of hardware and system configuration?
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: dxdiag also shows graphics and sound details.

questions.question: An NVMe SSD is faster than a SATA SSD mainly because it:

options.C: Connects over PCI Express lanes instead of the SATA interface (limited to about 600 MB/s)

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: PCIe 3.0 ×4 NVMe drives reach about 3,500 MB/s; PCIe 4.0 ×4 about 7,000 MB/s.

questions.question: Integrated graphics differ from a dedicated graphics card because integrated graphics:

options.B: Are built into the CPU/chipset and share system RAM

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: Dedicated cards have their own video memory (VRAM).

questions.question: Which of these is a minimum hardware requirement for Windows 11?
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: Windows 11 requires a 64-bit CPU, 4 GB RAM, 64 GB storage, UEFI Secure Boot capability and TPM 2.0.

questions.question: A monitor described as '24-inch' is measured:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: Screen size is the diagonal.

questions.question: In a configuration 'RAM: 16 GB DDR4-3200 (2 × 8 GB)', the '2 × 8 GB' means:

options.B: Two modules of 8 GB, allowing dual-channel operation

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: Two identical modules in the correct slots run in dual channel.

questions.question: A processor's 'base clock 2.5 GHz, boost 4.4 GHz' means that:

options.A: It runs at 2.5 GHz normally and can increase up to 4.4 GHz when thermal and power limits allow

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: Turbo/boost raises the clock dynamically under load.

questions.question: Which storage configuration gives the fastest boot times?

options.A: OS on a USB 2.0 pen drive
options.B: OS on a 1 TB 5400 RPM HDD
options.D: OS on a 512 GB NVMe SSD

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: NVMe SSDs have very low latency and high throughput.

questions.question: The Performance tab of Windows Task Manager shows:

options.B: Live usage of CPU, memory, disk, network and GPU

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: It also shows details such as cores, speed and memory slots used.

questions.question: A laptop processor with the suffix 'U' (e.g. i5-1235U) is designed for:

options.C: Low power consumption and long battery life

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: U-series chips have low TDP for thin laptops.

questions.question: How many pixels does a 1366 × 768 display have?
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System

questions.question: Which port is commonly used to connect a modern monitor carrying digital video and audio?
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: DisplayPort is another digital option; VGA is analog video only.

questions.question: A computer with '1 TB HDD + 256 GB SSD' storage typically uses:

options.A: The HDD for the OS and the SSD for backups
options.B: The SSD for the OS and programs, and the HDD for bulk data
options.D: The SSD as a CD drive

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: The fast SSD speeds up booting and applications while the HDD stores large files cheaply.

questions.question: Bluetooth is mainly used for:

options.B: Short-range wireless connection of devices like headsets, mice and phones

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: Its typical range is about 10 m.

questions.question: The L3 cache size in a processor specification refers to:

options.C: The shared last-level cache memory on the CPU

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: A larger L3 reduces trips to main memory.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A 64-bit OS can run on a 64-bit processor.
II. A 64-bit OS can run on a 32-bit-only processor.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: A 32-bit-only processor cannot execute 64-bit code.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Adding more RAM can make a computer faster when many programs are open.
Reason (R): With too little RAM, the OS must frequently move pages to the slower disk (paging).

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: More RAM reduces paging to disk.

questions.question: A GPU with '8 GB GDDR6' refers to:

options.D: The graphics card's dedicated video memory

questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: VRAM stores textures and frame buffers.

questions.question: Which of these most directly determines how many applications can stay open smoothly?
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: RAM holds the working data of running programs.

questions.question: The typical 'Configuration' of a school computer lab PC would NOT normally include:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: Supercomputer interconnects are only used in HPC clusters.

questions.question: SATA III interface supports a maximum transfer rate of:
questions.subject: Typical Configuration of a Computer System
questions.explanation: About 600 MB/s after encoding overhead.

questions.question: The motherboard is also known as the:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Apple calls it a logic board; IBM used 'planar'.

questions.question: The ATX form factor was introduced in 1995 by:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: ATX replaced the older IBM AT form factor.

questions.question: Which motherboard form factor is the smallest of these?
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Mini-ITX is 170 × 170 mm.

questions.question: The dimensions of a standard ATX motherboard are about:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Micro-ATX is 244 × 244 mm; E-ATX is larger than ATX.

questions.question: Which form factor was developed by VIA Technologies for small, low-power systems?
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Mini-ITX appeared in 2001.

questions.question: Compared with AT, the ATX form factor introduced:

options.A: Physical mains switches on the PSU
options.B: Soft power control (power on/off from the motherboard via PS_ON and +5VSB)

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: ATX allows the OS to shut down the computer and supports Wake-on-LAN.

questions.question: The BTX form factor, introduced by Intel in 2004, aimed mainly to:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: BTX was later abandoned.

questions.question: In LGA (Land Grid Array) sockets used by Intel, the pins are located:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: In PGA sockets (e.g. AMD AM4) the pins are on the CPU.

questions.question: AMD's AM4 socket uses ______, while AM5 uses ______.
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: AM5 moved to an LGA-1718 design.

questions.question: In most laptops, the CPU is attached to the motherboard using:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Ball Grid Array packages are soldered, so they are not user-replaceable.

questions.question: An 'integrated' motherboard is one that:

options.D: Has on-board components such as graphics, sound and network controllers

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Non-integrated boards rely on add-on cards for these functions.

questions.question: The chipset of a motherboard mainly determines:

options.A: Supported features such as CPU compatibility, number of USB/SATA ports, PCIe lanes and overclocking

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: For example, Intel Z-series chipsets allow CPU overclocking while B-series usually do not.

questions.question: The old AT motherboards used which keyboard connector?
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: ATX boards moved to PS/2 and later USB.

questions.question: AT power supplies connected to the motherboard using the:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Connecting P8/P9 the wrong way round could damage the board.

questions.question: LPX and NLX form factors are known for using a:

options.D: Riser card on which expansion cards are mounted parallel to the motherboard

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: They were used in slim desktop cases.

questions.question: Server motherboards typically differ from desktop boards by supporting:

options.B: Multiple CPU sockets and ECC/registered memory

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Reliability and scalability are key for servers.

questions.question: Most motherboards are made as:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Several copper layers carry power and signal traces.

questions.question: A passive board that only provides expansion slots, with the CPU on a plug-in card, is called a:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Backplanes are used in industrial and server systems.

questions.question: Which statement about Micro-ATX boards is correct?

options.B: They usually fit in ATX cases but have fewer expansion slots
options.C: They cannot fit in ATX cases

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Mounting holes are compatible with ATX cases.

questions.question: A small add-on circuit board that plugs into the motherboard to add functions is called a:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Graphics and sound cards are daughterboards.

questions.question: Branded PCs from some manufacturers often use:

options.B: Proprietary motherboard form factors that may limit upgrades

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Proprietary layouts can restrict replacement parts.

questions.question: The main function of the motherboard is to:

options.A: Interconnect and allow communication among the CPU, memory, storage and peripherals, and distribute power

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: It is the backbone that connects all components.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. AT motherboards supported soft power control through a PS_ON signal.
II. ATX motherboards have I/O ports built onto the rear edge, covered by an I/O shield.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Soft power control was introduced with ATX; statement II is correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Any Intel desktop processor fits any motherboard that has an LGA socket.
Reason (R): The socket type and chipset determine which processors a motherboard supports.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: A is false: LGA sockets differ (e.g. LGA1200 and LGA1700 are incompatible). R is true.

questions.question: E-ATX motherboards are mainly used in:

options.C: High-end workstations and enthusiast or server builds

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Extended ATX provides more slots and space.

questions.question: Which of these is a motherboard manufacturer?
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: ASUS, Gigabyte, MSI and ASRock are major motherboard makers.

questions.question: A ZIF socket stands for:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: A lever lets the CPU be inserted without force.

questions.question: Which motherboard form factor would you choose for a very compact home-theatre PC?
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Mini-ITX boards fit small cases.

questions.question: The motherboard of a Mac computer is called a:
questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: Apple uses the term logic board.

questions.question: Which statement about BGA packages is correct?

options.A: They are soldered to the board, saving space in thin devices
options.B: They are easily replaceable by users
options.D: They are used only in servers

questions.subject: Motherboard: Introduction and Types
questions.explanation: BGA is common in laptops and phones.

questions.question: In older chipsets, the northbridge was also called the:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: The southbridge was the I/O Controller Hub.

questions.question: In modern Intel systems, the southbridge functions are provided by the:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: The memory controller moved into the CPU.

questions.question: The CMOS on a motherboard stores:

options.C: BIOS/UEFI configuration settings such as boot order and date/time

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: The CMOS battery keeps these settings and the real-time clock when the PC is off.

questions.question: The coin cell commonly used as a CMOS battery is:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: It is a 3 V lithium cell.

questions.question: A 'Clear CMOS' jumper is used to:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Useful after wrong settings or a forgotten BIOS password.

questions.question: The VRM (Voltage Regulator Module) on a motherboard:

options.A: Converts 12 V to the low, stable voltage required by the CPU

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Good VRMs are important for high-power CPUs and overclocking.

questions.question: The main power connector from the PSU to an ATX motherboard has:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Modern boards use 24 pins; the CPU gets a separate 4/8-pin EPS connector.

questions.question: The 4/8-pin EPS12V connector near the CPU socket supplies power to:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: High-end boards may need two 8-pin connectors.

questions.question: Which slot is used for modern graphics cards?
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: AGP and ISA are obsolete; PCI is legacy.

questions.question: Approximately how much bandwidth does one PCIe 4.0 lane provide in each direction?
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: PCIe 3.0 ≈ 1 GB/s per lane, 4.0 ≈ 2 GB/s and 5.0 ≈ 4 GB/s.

questions.question: A PCIe 4.0 x16 slot provides roughly how much bandwidth in each direction?
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: 16 lanes × about 2 GB/s ≈ 32 GB/s.

questions.question: An M.2 slot with an 'M key' is typically used for:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: E-key M.2 slots are usually for Wi-Fi/Bluetooth cards.

questions.question: The BIOS/UEFI firmware is stored on the motherboard in a:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Flash allows BIOS updates (flashing).

questions.question: On the rear audio panel following the PC 99 colour code, the green jack is for:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Pink is microphone and light blue is line in.

questions.question: In the PC 99 colour code, PS/2 purple and green ports are for:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Purple = keyboard, green = mouse.

questions.question: The front-panel header on a motherboard connects:

options.C: The case's power button, reset button and power/HDD LEDs

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Pins are labelled PWR_SW, RESET_SW, PLED and HDD_LED.

questions.question: A 4-pin fan header differs from a 3-pin header because it:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: The fourth pin carries the PWM control signal.

questions.question: The crystal oscillator on the motherboard is used to:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Clock generators derive CPU and bus clocks from it.

questions.question: SATA ports on the motherboard are used to connect:

options.C: Hard disks, SATA SSDs and optical drives

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Each device also needs a SATA power connector from the PSU.

questions.question: DIMM slots on a desktop motherboard hold:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Slots are often colour-coded by channel.

questions.question: Heat sinks on the motherboard are commonly placed over:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: These components generate heat.

questions.question: A TPM (Trusted Platform Module) provides:

options.C: Hardware-based security functions such as secure key storage

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0 (discrete or firmware).

questions.question: Internal USB headers on the motherboard are used to connect:

options.D: The front-panel USB ports of the case

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: They provide USB to the case's front ports.

questions.question: The printed copper lines connecting components on a motherboard are called:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Buses are formed by groups of traces.

questions.question: Which component on the motherboard temporarily stores electrical charge to smooth the power supply?
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Solid polymer capacitors are common on modern boards.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The CPU socket type must match the processor.
II. Any DDR generation of RAM fits in any DIMM slot.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: DDR generations have different notch positions and are not interchangeable.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Removing the CMOS battery for some time may reset the BIOS settings.
Reason (R): CMOS settings are held in memory powered by the battery when the PC is off.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Without power the stored settings are lost and defaults are loaded.

questions.question: The rear I/O panel of a motherboard with integrated graphics typically includes:

options.A: HDMI/DisplayPort, USB, Ethernet (RJ-45) and audio jacks

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: These are the external connectors of the board.

questions.question: A POST code display (debug LED) on a motherboard helps to:

options.C: Identify the stage at which the boot process fails

questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: Each code corresponds to a POST step.

questions.question: The legacy PCI bus (32-bit, 33 MHz) has a peak bandwidth of about:
questions.subject: Components of the Motherboard
questions.explanation: 32 bits × 33 MHz = 4 bytes × 33.3 million ≈ 133 MB/s.

questions.question: Memory modules used in laptops are called:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: SO-DIMM (Small Outline DIMM) is about half the length of a desktop DIMM.

questions.question: A DDR4 desktop DIMM has how many pins?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: DDR = 184, DDR2 and DDR3 = 240, DDR4 and DDR5 = 288.

questions.question: The standard operating voltage of DDR4 memory is:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: DDR2 = 1.8 V, DDR3 = 1.5 V, DDR4 = 1.2 V, DDR5 = 1.1 V.

questions.question: DDR3 and DDR4 modules cannot be interchanged because:

options.C: Their notch positions, pin counts and voltages differ

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: The notch prevents inserting the wrong type.

questions.question: A distinctive feature of DDR5 modules is:

options.C: An on-module power management IC (PMIC) and two independent sub-channels per module

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Moving power regulation onto the module improves signal integrity.

questions.question: ECC memory can:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: ECC is common in servers and workstations.

questions.question: What is the true CAS latency, in nanoseconds, of DDR4-3200 CL16?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Latency = CL × 2000 / data rate = 16 × 2000 / 3200 = 10 ns.

questions.question: Intel XMP profiles are used to:

options.D: Automatically apply the memory's rated higher speed and timings

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: AMD's equivalent is EXPO.

questions.question: How many address lines are needed for a 1K × 8 memory chip?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: 1K = 1024 = 2^10 locations, so 10 address lines; 8 data lines carry each byte.

questions.question: How many 1K × 4 chips are needed to build a 4K × 8 memory?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Total bits: (4K × 8) / (1K × 4) = 8 chips (2 per row for 8 bits, 4 rows for 4K).

questions.question: A byte-addressable memory of 64 KB needs how many address lines?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: 64 KB = 2^16 bytes.

questions.question: A 256K × 8 memory chip has a capacity of:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: 256K locations × 1 byte = 256 KB = 2,097,152 bits.

questions.question: To build a 4K × 8 memory from four 1K × 8 chips, the chip-select signals are generated using a:

options.D: 2-to-4 decoder driven by the two highest address lines

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: 12 address lines are needed: 10 go to every chip and 2 select one of the four chips.

questions.question: Dual-channel memory operation mainly increases:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Two 64-bit channels transfer data in parallel.

questions.question: The Windows 'paging file' (pagefile.sys) is used for:

options.A: Virtual memory: storing pages of memory on disk when RAM is full

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Linux uses a swap partition or swap file.

questions.question: SIMM modules, used in older PCs, had connectors that were:

options.B: Redundant on both sides of the module (same signals)

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: DIMMs have separate contacts on each side, allowing a wider data path.

questions.question: RIMM modules were used with:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: RDRAM was used by some Pentium 4 systems.

questions.question: Which statement about installing RAM is correct?

options.A: The notch must align with the key in the slot, and the clips lock when fully inserted
options.B: RAM must be installed while the PC is on
options.D: Modules can be inserted either way round

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Incorrect alignment can damage the module or slot.

questions.question: Registered (buffered) memory is mainly used in:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: A register buffers signals, allowing more modules per channel.

questions.question: The effective data rate of DDR memory is twice its I/O clock because:

options.D: It transfers data on both rising and falling clock edges

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Hence 'Double Data Rate'.

questions.question: Which type of memory is used as the main system RAM in PCs?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: SRAM is used for caches.

questions.question: A DDR4 SO-DIMM has how many pins?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: DDR3 SO-DIMM = 204 pins; DDR4 SO-DIMM = 260; DDR5 SO-DIMM = 262.

questions.question: If a PC has 8 GB of RAM installed but shows only about 3.2 GB usable, the most likely reason is:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: 32-bit Windows can use at most about 3–4 GB.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Memory modules of different speeds usually run at the speed of the slowest module.
II. Mixing different capacities always prevents booting.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Different capacities often work (sometimes without full dual channel); mismatched speeds fall back to the slowest.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): SRAM is used for cache memory.
Reason (R): SRAM is cheaper and denser than DRAM.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: A is true, but R is false: SRAM is costlier and less dense. It is used for cache because it is faster and needs no refresh.

questions.question: How many bits does a standard (non-ECC) DDR4 DIMM transfer per memory transfer?
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: ECC DIMMs are 72 bits wide (64 data + 8 check bits).

questions.question: The time taken to access data from DRAM is typically in the range of:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: Disk access is in milliseconds, which is why RAM is so much faster.

questions.question: Increasing RAM from 4 GB to 16 GB mainly helps a computer to:

options.A: Run more and larger programs simultaneously without slow paging

questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: RAM is working memory.

questions.question: Memory 'CL' in module specifications stands for:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: It is the number of clock cycles between a column command and data availability.

questions.question: A computer has 4 DIMM slots and supports up to 64 GB. The largest module size it can use in each slot is most likely:
questions.subject: Memory
questions.explanation: 64 GB ÷ 4 slots = 16 GB per slot.

sets.name: 2 · Power Supply to the Computer System

questions.question: A computer's SMPS is preferred over a linear power supply because it is:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: High-frequency switching allows small transformers and higher efficiency.

questions.question: In an ATX power supply, the yellow wires carry:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Red = +5 V, orange = +3.3 V, black = ground.

questions.question: In an ATX power supply, the red wires carry:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Red is the +5 V rail.

questions.question: The green wire (PS_ON#) of the ATX connector:

options.A: Turns the PSU on when pulled to ground

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Shorting green to black is used to test a PSU.

questions.question: The purple wire (+5VSB) in an ATX PSU provides:

options.B: Standby power even when the PC is off, for features like wake-on-LAN

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It keeps soft-power circuits alive.

questions.question: The grey 'Power Good' (PWR_OK) signal tells the motherboard that:

options.B: The PSU outputs have stabilised and it is safe to start

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: The board holds the CPU in reset until this signal arrives.

questions.question: A standard PCIe 8-pin power connector is rated for:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: A 6-pin connector is rated 75 W and the PCIe x16 slot itself supplies up to 75 W.

questions.question: A graphics card with one 8-pin PCIe connector plus slot power can draw a maximum of about:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System

questions.question: SATA power connectors have how many pins?
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: They supply 3.3 V, 5 V and 12 V to SATA drives.

questions.question: The 4-pin Molex connector is traditionally used to power:

options.A: Older IDE drives, fans and peripherals

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It carries +5 V and +12 V.

questions.question: An '80 PLUS Gold' PSU is:

options.A: More efficient than an 80 PLUS Bronze PSU

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Levels in order: White, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Titanium.

questions.question: A modular power supply:

options.D: Allows unused cables to be detached, improving airflow and neatness

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Semi-modular PSUs have some fixed cables.

questions.question: A UPS rated 1000 VA with a power factor of 0.6 can supply a real load of about:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Watts = VA × power factor = 1000 × 0.6 = 600 W.

questions.question: Which UPS type has zero transfer time because the load always runs from the inverter?
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It continuously converts AC → DC → AC.

questions.question: A line-interactive UPS includes an AVR, which:

options.C: Corrects moderate voltage fluctuations without switching to battery

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Automatic Voltage Regulation saves battery life.

questions.question: A 12 V, 7 Ah UPS battery stores about how much energy?
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Energy = 12 V × 7 Ah = 84 Wh (ideal).

questions.question: Ignoring losses, how long could an 84 Wh battery run a 42 W load?
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: 84 Wh ÷ 42 W = 2 hours; real backup is shorter because of inverter losses.

questions.question: A surge protector mainly protects equipment against:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It does not provide backup power.

questions.question: The standard mains supply in India is:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: PSUs sold in India must support 230 V AC.

questions.question: When choosing PSU wattage, it is recommended to:

options.B: Match exactly the total component power
options.D: Add headroom (e.g. 20–30%) above the estimated peak load

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Headroom improves efficiency, stability and future upgrades.

questions.question: Active PFC in a power supply:

options.A: Improves the power factor, drawing current more efficiently from the mains

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It reduces reactive power and harmonics.

questions.question: The −12 V rail in an ATX PSU is carried by the:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It is rarely used by modern components.

questions.question: Which statement about an offline (standby) UPS is correct?

options.A: It powers the load from the inverter all the time
options.B: It switches to battery only when mains power fails, with a short transfer time
options.D: It is the most expensive type

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It is common for home PCs.

questions.question: The newer 12VHPWR (16-pin) connector on high-end graphics cards can deliver up to:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It was introduced with the ATX 3.0 specification.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A voltage stabiliser provides backup power during outages.
II. A surge protector provides backup power during outages.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Neither provides backup power; only a UPS (with a battery) does.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A higher-efficiency PSU produces less heat.
Reason (R): Less input power is wasted as heat to deliver the same output power.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Losses in a PSU appear mostly as heat.

questions.question: A PSU delivers 400 W to the components at 80% efficiency. How much power does it draw from the wall?
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Input = output / efficiency = 400 / 0.8 = 500 W.

questions.question: The orange wires in an ATX power supply carry:
questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Orange = +3.3 V.

questions.question: A 'paperclip test' on an ATX PSU involves:

options.D: Shorting the green PS_ON wire to a black ground wire to switch the PSU on without a motherboard

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: It checks whether the PSU powers on; it must be done carefully with the PSU unplugged while connecting.

questions.question: Why must a PSU never be opened by an untrained person even when unplugged?

options.A: Its large capacitors can hold a dangerous charge

questions.subject: Power Supply to the Computer System
questions.explanation: Stored charge can cause serious electric shock.

questions.question: Before handling computer components, you should first:

options.B: Apply thermal paste to your hands
options.D: Discharge static electricity, e.g. by using an anti-static wrist strap

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Electrostatic discharge can destroy chips.

questions.question: When installing an Intel LGA CPU, you should:

options.B: Apply thermal paste under the CPU
options.C: Align the triangle/notches, place it gently without force, then close the retention lever

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: LGA socket pins are delicate and bend easily.

questions.question: How much thermal paste is typically applied to a desktop CPU?

options.A: A pea-sized amount in the centre of the CPU
options.C: A thick layer covering the motherboard

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Mounting pressure spreads it; too much can overflow.

questions.question: The CPU cooler fan cable should be connected to the motherboard header labelled:
questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Many boards refuse to boot or warn if CPU_FAN reads no speed.

questions.question: Standoffs are installed in the case before mounting the motherboard to:

options.D: Keep the board raised so its underside does not short against the metal case

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Standoffs must match the board's mounting holes.

questions.question: The I/O shield is installed:

options.B: In the case's rear opening before mounting the motherboard

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Some boards come with a pre-installed shield.

questions.question: A graphics card is normally installed in the:

options.D: Top-most PCIe x16 slot (connected to the CPU lanes)

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: It also needs PCIe power connectors if required.

questions.question: A monitor connected to the motherboard's HDMI port shows no display, although a graphics card is installed. The likely fix is to:

options.A: Connect the monitor to the graphics card's output port

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: When a dedicated GPU is present, integrated graphics output is often disabled.

questions.question: Case front-panel connectors include:

options.A: PWR_SW, RESET_SW, POWER LED and HDD LED

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: LED connectors have polarity (+/−).

questions.question: Which is the usual airflow arrangement in a PC case?

options.C: Front (and bottom) fans intake, rear and top fans exhaust
options.D: Front fans exhaust, rear fans intake

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: This follows the natural rise of hot air.

questions.question: For dual-channel operation with two RAM modules on a four-slot board, you should usually:

options.B: Use slots 1 and 2 next to each other
options.C: Use the slots recommended in the manual (often A2 and B2)

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: The manual shows the correct slot pairs.

questions.question: Which key is commonly pressed during start-up to enter the BIOS/UEFI setup?

options.A: Del or F2 (depending on the manufacturer)

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: F12 or F8/F11 often open a boot menu instead.

questions.question: After assembling a PC and booting for the first time, you should first:

options.D: Check in BIOS/UEFI that the CPU, RAM and drives are detected correctly

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Then set the boot order and install the OS.

questions.question: An operating system is usually installed on a new PC from:

options.D: A bootable USB drive or DVD

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Set the boot device in BIOS or use the one-time boot menu.

questions.question: After installing the OS, the next important step is to:
questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Drivers ensure devices work correctly.

questions.question: Which tool is most commonly needed to assemble a PC?
questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Most case, board and drive screws are Phillips.

questions.question: When a newly assembled PC powers on but shows no display and gives repeated beeps, the first component to check is usually:
questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Beep codes vary by vendor, but memory problems are a common cause.

questions.question: Components such as RAM and expansion cards should be held:
questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Touching contacts leaves oil and risks ESD damage.

questions.question: An M.2 NVMe SSD is secured on the motherboard using:

options.B: A small screw or latch at the end of the slot

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Some boards use tool-less latches.

questions.question: Good cable management in a PC mainly helps to:

options.C: Improve airflow and make maintenance easier

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Neat cables do not block airflow.

questions.question: Which connection must be made for a SATA hard disk to work?

options.B: Both the SATA data cable (to the motherboard) and the SATA power cable (from the PSU)

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Data and power are separate connections.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The PC should be unplugged from mains while installing components.
II. Thermal paste is applied between the CPU and the socket.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Thermal paste goes between the CPU's heat spreader and the cooler, not into the socket.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Installing the CPU and RAM before fixing the motherboard in the case is recommended.
Reason (R): Motherboards are made as multi-layer printed circuit boards.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Both are true, but R does not explain A; the reason is that an open board gives more working space and less risk of damage.

questions.question: Overclocking a CPU means:

options.A: Running it above its rated speed, usually with more heat and power
options.D: Running it below its rated speed

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: It requires good cooling and a suitable motherboard.

questions.question: The main reason for applying the BIOS setting 'XMP/EXPO' after assembly is to:

options.B: Enable the RAM to run at its advertised speed

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Without it, RAM runs at default JEDEC speeds.

questions.question: If the PC does not power on at all after assembly, a likely cause is:

options.B: The front-panel power switch connector is not connected correctly, or the PSU switch is off

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Check the PSU switch, power cable and PWR_SW header first.

questions.question: Which order is correct for a typical PC build?

options.A: Mount motherboard in case → install CPU → apply paste → install PSU
options.B: Install OS → install CPU → install RAM
options.C: Connect monitor → install CPU → install case
options.D: Install CPU, cooler and RAM on the board → mount board in case → install PSU and drives → connect cables → first boot

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: This minimises risk and effort.

questions.question: An anti-static bag is used for:

options.A: Storing and carrying electronic components safely

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: It shields components from static charges.

questions.question: Why should the CPU cooler be mounted with even pressure on all corners?

options.A: To ensure good, uniform contact for heat transfer and avoid damaging the CPU

questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: Tightening screws diagonally in steps is recommended.

questions.question: POST stands for:
questions.subject: Assembling the Computer System
questions.explanation: It checks basic hardware before the OS loads.
